profile.headline: Java Champion, Kotlin fanatic, and Senior Software Engineer at Datadog. Morphia maintainer.
profile.geoLocationName: New York, New York, United States
profile.summary:
I have decades of experience building software from database drivers all the way up event services and integrations of external resourcs to core services.  In addition to my day job responsibilities, I'm also an active speaker at technical conferences and user groups around the world.  In addition, I'm an active contributor to  several open source projects and the current maintainer of MongoDB mapping library Morphia.  

Learning is a key goal for me so I'm not afraid to tackle new projects in unfamiliar spaces whether that's new problem domains or new programming languages. I enjoy sharing what I've learned both on the conference circuit when I can and through mentorship roles, tech meetups, and informal settings with coworkers. Community and inclusion is a big focus of mine and I'm much more interested in getting things done than getting the credit.   ...  Though, getting credit is awfully nice, too.

projects.title: Morphia
projects.description: Morphia is an Object Document Mapper for the JVM.  Much like JPA/Hibernate and other ORMs in the relational world, an ODM maps between and applications Java types and the driver primitives necessary to read and store data using MongoDB rather than a traditional relational database.

organizations.name: Basement Coders
organizations.description:
http://www.basementcoders.com

A Developers Podcast with an organic agenda delivered with colorful language. Although we primarily focus on what's happening in the realm of the JVM, we have been known to investigate other platforms and languages, essentially anything which might pique our interest. We've done everything from interviewing James Gosling to discussing why every office environment seems to have a developer who smells like they haven't bathed in a week.
